row.evidence: Spree's docs say OpenID Connect single sign-on is built into the open-source core, and staff are managed through the dashboard and the Admin API; no SCIM endpoint appears in the docs, the Admin API OpenAPI spec or the Enterprise Edition comparison.
row.notes: Spree Commerce is open-source (BSD-3/MIT) self-hosted e-commerce software. Community Edition is free; Enterprise Edition is a commercial licence with custom pricing (contact us), so no per-user prices exist. Staff SSO via OpenID Connect ships in core (the Enterprise page's comparison table ticks SSO for both editions); custom auth strategies can auto-provision users on first login. Staff lifecycle is scriptable through the Admin API v3 (list/update/remove staff, invitations, roles) with a secret API key and read_staff/write_staff scopes, but there is no SCIM endpoint. Audit trail is Enterprise-only.

plans.name: Community Edition
plans.notes: Self-hosted. SSO via OpenID Connect in core; Admin API included. Audit trail not included. SCIM false = not documented in any edition.

plans.name: Enterprise Edition
plans.price_text: Custom Pricing (Enterprise License Agreement); get in touch for pricing
plans.notes: Adds audit trail, private cloud, HIPAA-ready deployment and dedicated support. No audit-log API endpoint found.

scim.notes: available=false by absence: no SCIM in the docs sitemap, llms.txt indexes, Admin API OpenAPI spec or Enterprise Edition page.

capabilities.notes: Staff are added by invitation (no direct create). DELETE removes the staff member's role assignments on the store and preserves the account, so it acts as store-level deactivation, not account deletion.

endpoints.purpose: Update a staff member (name fields, role_ids)
Remove a staff member from this store

user_api.notes: Other documented staff endpoints (from the Admin API OpenAPI spec): GET /api/v3/admin/admin_users/{id}, GET/DELETE invitations, POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/v3/admin/roles, GET /api/v3/admin/permissions.

fallbacks.notes: JIT is how custom auth strategies behave (find_or_create on first login); docs describe it on the Store API with a one-line Admin swap.
